Occurrence Remarks: [All these qualities can be observed within the photographs.] Firstly, this plant has distinct qualities of the Fabaceae family; woody shrub, legumes as fruit and flowers with 5 free petals. This plant is of the Fabaceae subfamily, Caesalpinioideae as the flowers are irregular with a non-papilionaceous corolla and equally sized petals. Secondly, it has distinct qualities of the Genus Senna; absent spines/prickles, pinnately compound leaves, yellow petals and flat dehiscent pods. Thirdly, it has distinct qualities of the species Senna didymobotrya; 7-15 leaflet pairs per leaf, absent glands on leaves, tall raceme inflorescence with dark brown bracts, 2 conspicuous anthers and oblong pods with depressions between the seeds. All other Senna species do not have as tall of a raceme and have much lighter coloured bracts. Extra info: This plant is commonly referred to as the popcorn plant as rubbing the leaves will bring about the scent of buttered popcorn, however, it does depend on the person. References include Field Guide to the Native Plants by Les Robinson (2003) and PlantNET. Photographed during the day.
